title: 057 Docker Compose Commands

segments.text: In the last section we spoke about how Docker compose automatically sets up some networking between these different services or these different types of containers that we define inside of our Docker compose file.
Now that all of stuff is supposedly set up, let's figure out how to start up Docker compose using this file.
Alright, so remember the entire purpose or well I should say one of the purposes of Docker compose is to kind of make it easier to run all the different commands that you usually run with Docker run.
So whereas before we would start up a new instance of a container using Docker run and then the name of the image that we want to create the container out of.
To create a instance of all the containers or all the images or all the services listed inside of our compose file we're going to run the command Docker dash compose up.
Now that one's pretty straightforward so essentially instead of saying run we're going to say up and we don't have to specify an image.
We're not specifying an image because Docker compose is going to look into our current working directory and automatically look for a Docker dash compose file inside there.
Now the thing to be aware of is that before we have the two separate Docker commands to build an image and run it.
So if we wanted to rebuild the image from our Docker file and then start an instance of it two separate commands.

But in the Docker compose world if we ever want to rebuild the images that are listed inside of our Docker compose file for example if we wanted to have Docker compose rebuild this container right here where the image use for that container.
We write Docker compose up dash dash built.

And so this dash dash build right here is what essentially tells Docker compose start up our containers again, but make sure you try to rebuild them ahead of time so that we get all the latest changes.
Okay, so let's get this shot I'm going to flip on over to my terminal.
I'm inside of my project directory and I can definitely verify that I have my Docker dash compose file inside of here.
So I'm going to run Docker dash compose up.
Now I want you to take a look at the very first line right here the very first line says creating network visits underscore default.

So like I said before when you just create a new set of containers or services with Docker compose it's going to automatically make a network for you that's going to join those different containers together.
After that we can see that it is creating an image for our node application.
And then if we scroll down a little bit more we're going to see a whole bunch of different output down here.
The most important lines to see are creating visits node app one.
So that's a single instance of our node dash app service.
And then we've got a single instance of our redness server as well.
After that we'll then start to see all the output from both of those different services start to appear.
So every line here that's appearing in yellow for me is output from the redness server.
And if I scroll down a little bit more I'll eventually see some output from the node application.
So it looks like based on ready to accept connections right here and listing import eighty eighty one right here definitely looks like both of our containers set up were created successfully.
So let's open up our browser we're going to try to open up our node application and see if the entire app works.
All right so I'm going to open up local host.
For a thousand in one remember when we made that kind of last minute change there we had hard coded to say port eighty eighty one.
But the last minute we decided to change the port used to four thousand one so make sure you go into local host colon four thousand one.
And then sure enough we see number visits is zero.
And then we can refresh and every time that we refresh the page we'll see that number of visits start to increment.
Awesome.
That's a basic usage of Docker compose we created two separate services and Docker compose automatically made connections between the two available.
The real key thing to keep in mind here is that in order to communicate between the two we used a host name of the name of that other service or that other container that was created.
And that name is specified inside of our Docker compose file right here.
And you are making use of maybe some database driver inside of your web application layer anywhere you would normally put in a connection URL or connection your eye.
You can instead just list the name of that other container and the host name will be automatically resolved for you by Docker.
All right.
